To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the strength of the C IV absorption is a strong, non-linear function of both the H I optical-depth (and thus the gas density), and the presence of galaxies in the vicinity of the line of sight, and that the metallicity in the intergalactic medium at z ~ 2.8 is enhanced in regions that are close to galaxies, but is likely to be widespread.

the metal line optical depth is a strong function not only of H I optical depth but also of proximity to galaxies, but that the enrichment of the intergalactic medium is widespread, and not confined to regions close to galaxies.

(1) the metallicity of gas in the IGM is a function of proximity to galaxies, (2) this metallicity gradient is a strong function both of the gas density and proximity to galaxies, and (3) the metallicity gradient is not a simple function of gas density alone.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the metal enrichment of the intergalactic medium, the spatial distribution of metals in the IGM, the relationship between the IGM and the galaxies that are thought to enrich it, and the relationship between the metal content of the IGM and its H I density.
the distribution of metals in the intergalactic medium (IGM).
the spatial distribution of metals in the diffuse intergalatic medium.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

while the metal line absorption in the diffuse intergalatic medium is a strong function not only of gas density but also proximity to galaxies, there is no evidence of a significant contribution from metal lines produced only in the vicinity of galaxies.
the metallicity of intergalactic gas is a strong function not only of gas density (and thus proximity to galaxies) but also of proximity to highly enriched galaxies.
the metal enrichment of the IGM is a function of both gas density and proximity to galaxies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the metals are more widely spread than galaxies but that there are still strong spatial variations.
the metallicity in the IGM increases with both the gas density and the proximity to galaxies.
the metallicity of intergalactic gas at high redshift is a function of both the gas density and the proximity to galaxies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the metallicity in the intergalactic medium is not only dependent on gas density but also on the environment.
the spatial distribution of metallicity is a complex function of both the local density and the local environment.
